title: All one in Christ (Galatians 3:23–29)
hook: neither Jew nor Greek, slave nor free, male and female
tomorrow: is everyone a child of God, or do you have to be adopted?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a split table in Antioch and Paul's most personal line, said mid-argument: Christ lives in me. Today he answers the table with a sentence.
screen: `CHRIST LIVES IN ME.` → `THE TABLE GETS AN ANSWER.`

segments.voice: Every form has the boxes. Check one. Paul writes a sentence that knocks over three of them: "There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female." Neither, nor. Neither, nor. Neither, nor. That's the King James, an even drumbeat. But in Paul's Greek the drumbeat slips. The first two pairs are neither, nor. The third isn't neither male nor female. It's male and female. Why would a careful writer change the rhythm right at the end?
screen: `CHECK ONE BOX.` → `NEITHER, NOR. NEITHER, NOR.` → `THEN: MALE AND FEMALE.`

segments.voice: Those three words come from the first page of the Bible. Genesis says of human beings: "male and female created he them." Some readers hear Paul pointing straight back there. What God made in the beginning, God is now gathering into one family. That's the thing to tell a friend tonight: tucked inside a famous verse about unity is a quiet quotation from creation. Now look at how Paul gets to the line. "For ye are all the children of God by faith in Christ Jesus. For as many of you as have been baptized into Christ have put on Christ." Put on, like clothes. Everyone who comes up out of the water wears the same garment. Then the end of the sentence: "for ye are all one in Christ Jesus." Notice what that doesn't say. Paul goes on writing to Jews and Greeks, to slaves and free people, to women and men. The differences are still there; Galatians never asks anyone to stop being who they are. What's gone is the ranking. None of these lines decides who belongs at the table. And then the surprise for yesterday's outsiders: "if ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise." The Gentiles Peter wouldn't eat with turn out to be family, heirs to a promise made to Abraham.
screen: `MALE AND FEMALE CREATED HE THEM.` · `PUT ON CHRIST, LIKE CLOTHES.` · `DIFFERENT, NOT RANKED.` · `ABRAHAM'S SEED, HEIRS.` · then, large: `ALL ONE.`

segments.voice: Find a pen and a scrap of paper. Write the name of one person on the other side of a divide in your life, a family feud, a team, a faith, and under it one true thing you honor in them. Keep the paper where you'll see it this week.
All one in Christ. Paul's line for people who stay different, and stop ranking each other, in one family.
Keep this line: all one, which was never the same as all alike. Peace to you.

chat.meaning: Paul's all one in Christ Jesus doesn't erase Jew and Greek, women and men. It ends the ranking of who belongs.

notes: Written 2026-10-13 in the year-2-4 recipe (style pass and new-lesson data built in from the start).

Puzzle: the Greek of 3:28's third pair reads ἄρσεν καὶ θῆλυ ('male and female'), the wording of Genesis 1:27 in the Septuagint, while the first two pairs use οὐκ ἔνι … οὐδέ ('neither … nor'). The KJV smooths all three to 'neither … nor'. The voice quotes the KJV, then describes the Greek; 'some readers hear Paul pointing back' to creation is hedged. Please confirm.
The schoolmaster line (3:24) was cut from the voice for length; it remains in the paraphrased range 3:23–25.
'The differences are still there; what's gone is the ranking' is an interpretation; readers apply 3:28 in different ways in church and society, which the lesson leaves aside.
Unity thread: myth 1 notes honestly that 3:28 speaks of the baptized ('in Christ Jesus'), not every person on earth; tomorrow's debate takes up whether everyone is God's child.
howItsDone: confirm the white baptismal garment and the reading of Galatians 3:27 at some baptisms.
